# Plan: 002-cms-conteudo
<!-- Generated by /speckit.plan -->
<!-- Date: 2026-08-31 -->

## Research Notes

The Truth Map ([`research.md`](research.md)) found two things that **contradict the spec as
written**, and they shape everything below.

**1. There is no anonymous read path.** `scopedAccess` opens `if (!user) return false`, and
every scoped collection wires `read: scopedAccess()`. The public site has no session, so
FR-010 (published content is publicly listable) and FR-015 (anonymous downloads) are
unimplementable today. It is the same defect as feature 001's theme gap, where
`organizations.read = masterOnly()` hides a visitor's own organization from them. **One cause,
two symptoms, and this feature is where it gets fixed** — Sketch 2 is the centre of this plan.

**2. `clientUploads: true` cannot be validated by magic bytes**, and `tech-stack.md` said so
before this spec existed: browser → MinIO by presigned URL means *"o Node nunca vê os bytes."*
CLR-003's decision stands — verify by signature, never parse — but its mechanism moves to
**presigned + `HeadObject` + post-upload verification + quarantine**, which that document
already prescribes.

Two corrections to my own earlier reading, both from the code rather than from memory: the
per-organization role **does** exist (`PendingInvites` carries `admin | staff | maker` and
`invite.ts` reads `orgs[].role`), so FR-008's "lab team" is implementable; and Payload
authentication is already on (`Users` § `auth: true`), so `curtida` and `progressoAula` need
nothing from feature 004 — 004 adds the public sign-up UI, not authentication itself.

## Data Model

See [`data-model.md`](data-model.md). Thirteen collections, every field traced to a page spec's
*Modelo de conteúdo*. No migration is optional here: this is the feature that adds real tables,
so the drift gate from feature 000 is live throughout.

## API Contracts

No new HTTP surface is authored. Payload's REST and GraphQL are generated from the collections,
which is precisely why **access control is the contract** — an access function that returns a
boolean instead of a constraint opens every generated endpoint at once.

## Implementation Approach

Order follows risk, not the collection list. The access layer lands first because every
collection depends on it, and getting it wrong is a cross-tenant leak rather than a bug.

1. **`publicRead()` and `teamOnly()`, with the harness extended before any content exists.**
2. **One collection end to end** (`projeto`) — registry entry, `sameTenant` relations, review
   queue, counters — as the template the other twelve follow.
3. **Uploads**, which are the only genuinely new subsystem: adapter, limits, quarantine, reaper.
4. **The remaining collections**, mechanical once the template is proven.
5. **`payload-locked-documents`**, after there is real scoped content for it to leak.

**The thing most likely to go wrong quietly**: `publicRead()` widens read access to
unauthenticated requests. Every previous cross-tenant defect in this project has been a rule
that matched a form the problem did not take. This one is worse if wrong, because the failure
is silent and public.

## Code Sketches (Mental Alignment)

### Sketch 1: a scoped collection, and its registry entry

**File:** `apps/web/collections/content/Projeto.ts` (new)

```ts
export const Projeto: CollectionConfig = {
  slug: 'projeto',
  labels: { singular: 'Projeto', plural: 'Projetos' },
  access: {
    read: publicRead('projeto'),      // published rows to anyone; drafts to members
    create: scopedAccess(),
    update: scopedAccess(),
    delete: teamOnly(),
  },
  fields: [
    { name: 'titulo', type: 'text', required: true, label: 'Título' },
    { name: 'categoria', type: 'relationship', relationTo: 'categoriaProjeto',
      required: true, validate: sameTenant },
    { name: 'status', type: 'select', required: true, defaultValue: 'rascunho',
      options: REVIEW_STATES, access: { update: teamOnlyField } },
  ],
}
```

**Why this shape:** the registry entry (`{ scope: 'scoped', why: '…' }`) is what
`registry.test.ts` demands, and `sameTenant` is what stops a project pointing at another
organization's category. `status` carries **field-level** access so a maker may edit their own
draft but not publish it — the alternative, guarding the transition in a hook, is checked after
the write is already shaped.

### Sketch 2: `publicRead` — the anonymous, host-scoped reader

**File:** `apps/web/lib/tenancy/access.ts` (modify)
**Intent:** the one addition that makes a public site possible without weakening isolation.

```ts
export const publicRead = (collection: string): Access => async ({ req }) => {
  const user = req?.user as MaybeUser
  if (isMaster(user)) return true

  // Anonymous, or a member of some OTHER organization browsing this host: both are visitors
  // here, and both see exactly the published rows of the organization the HOST resolves to.
  const org = await resolveTenant(hostOf(req))
  if (!org) return false                              // unresolved host reads nothing
  const published: Where = { tenant: { equals: org.id }, status: { equals: 'publicado' } }

  const ids = tenantIdsOf(user)
  if (ids.length === 0) return published
  /* @isolation-mutation-point */
  return { or: [published, { tenant: { in: ids } }] } as Where
}
```

**Why this shape:** it keeps feature 000's contract — **a query constraint, never a boolean** —
and adds the axis the original lacked: *the host*, not just the session. A visitor sees
published rows of the organization whose hostname they typed; a member additionally sees their
own organization's drafts. The `or` is the whole design: without it a signed-in maker of lab A
visiting lab B would see nothing, and with a naive `if (!user)` it would be two divergent code
paths that drift.

The `@isolation-mutation-point` marker is deliberate — `scripts/isolation-mutation.sh` breaks
marked lines and requires the harness to notice, so this line joins the set that must be proven
breakable.

### Sketch 3: `teamOnly` — who may publish

**File:** `apps/web/lib/tenancy/access.ts` (modify)

```ts
/** `admin` and `staff` are the lab team; `maker` submits and cannot publish (FR-008). */
export const teamOnly = (): Access => ({ req }) => {
  const user = req?.user as MaybeUser
  if (isMaster(user)) return true
  const teamOrgs = (user?.orgs ?? [])
    .filter((row) => row?.role === 'admin' || row?.role === 'staff')
    .map(idOf)
  return teamOrgs.length > 0 ? ({ tenant: { in: teamOrgs } } as Where) : false
}
```

**Why this shape:** the role already exists — `PendingInvites` offers `admin | staff | maker`
and `invite.ts` reads `orgs[].role`. `access.ts`'s own `MaybeUser` type omits it, which is why
it looked absent; widening that type is part of this change. Returning a constraint rather than
`true` means a staff member of lab A cannot publish lab B's content even if a route forgets to
check.

### Sketch 4: uploads — presigned, then verified, then released

**File:** `apps/web/lib/uploads/verify.ts` (new)

```ts
/** Runs AFTER the browser has uploaded straight to the bucket. `beforeValidate` cannot:
 *  with clientUploads the bytes never reach Node (tech-stack.md § Absorções, item 3). */
export async function verifyUploaded(key: string, declared: MediaGroup): Promise<VerifyResult> {
  const head = await s3.headObject(key)
  if (head.ContentLength > CAP[declared]) return reject('excede o limite', head.ContentLength)

  const firstBytes = await s3.getRange(key, 0, SIGNATURE_WINDOW)   // a few KB, never the file
  if (!signatureMatches(firstBytes, declared)) return reject('conteúdo não confere com o tipo')

  return release(key)   // out of quarantine/ and into the served prefix
}
```

**Why this shape:** CLR-003 said verify by signature and never parse, and this is the only
mechanism that can. Objects land in a `quarantine/` prefix that is not publicly served; only a
passing check moves them. A `.glb` is confirmed to be a **container**, never a model — stated
in the spec so nobody later reads this as model validation.

### Sketch 5: the review transition, stamped once

**File:** `apps/web/lib/content/review.ts` (new)

```ts
export const stampApproval: CollectionBeforeChangeHook = ({ data, originalDoc }) => {
  const entering = data.status === 'publicado' && originalDoc?.status !== 'publicado'
  if (!entering || originalDoc?.aprovacaoRegistrada === true) return data
  // Set once, never cleared. Feature 005 reads this and writes the ledger (CLR-001);
  // clearing it on unpublish is what would let a republish credit a second time.
  return { ...data, aprovacaoRegistrada: true, aprovadoEm: new Date().toISOString() }
}
```

**Why this shape:** this feature writes **no XP**. It records that approval happened, once, in
the same write as the transition — so 005 can credit correctly for content approved before it
existed, with no backfill. SC-004's sequence (publish → unpublish → republish → one record) is
what proves the `aprovacaoRegistrada` guard rather than the `entering` guard alone.

### Sketch 6: `payload-locked-documents`, scoped

**File:** `apps/web/payload.config.ts` (modify)

```ts
// Feature 000 escalated this in writing: the collection references our scoped documents,
// the plugin does not compose access over it, and org B can enumerate org A's document IDs.
collections: [...ours],
// Payload exposes its internal collections for override; compose the same constraint.
onInit: composeAccessFor('payload-locked-documents', scopedAccess()),
```

**Why this shape:** CLR-004 chose scoping over denial so the admin keeps its "someone else is
editing this" warning, which matters for a team sharing one admin (US7). **The fallback is
denial**, and which one ships depends on whether Payload permits composing access on an
internal collection — a fact to establish with a spike, not an assumption. SC-003 requires
seeing the leak **fail first**, so the test is written against today's behaviour before the fix.

### Sketch 7: one counter strategy, and the drift it can produce

**File:** `apps/web/lib/content/counters.ts` (new)

```ts
/** Stored, maintained in the SAME transaction as the write that causes it. */
export const bumpCounter: CollectionAfterChangeHook = async ({ req, doc, operation }) => {
  await recount(req, doc.alvo, operation)   // inside req.transactionID, not after it
}
```

**Why this shape:** the alternative — counting on read — is an N+1 across every listing page,
and this design serves card grids. Storing it costs the classic failure, so the failure is
**named rather than hoped away**: a stored counter drifts the moment a row is created or
deleted by a path the hook does not see — an admin bulk delete, a migration, a manual SQL fix.

The mitigation is not "be careful". It is a **reconciliation test** that recomputes every
counter from its source rows and asserts equality, running in CI beside the isolation harness.
Same discipline as Principle 3's "XP is granted inside the same transaction as the action that
caused it", applied to counters.

`formatos` is derived rather than counted — extensions of `arquivosModelo`, computed on save —
but it obeys the same rule: derived at write, verified by the same reconciliation test.

## Constitution Compliance

- [x] **Principle 1 — Locked stack:** one runtime dependency added, `@payloadcms/storage-s3`,
  and it is **pre-sanctioned rather than newly argued**: `tech-stack.md` § Stack fixes object
  storage as *"S3-compatível: MinIO self-hosted ↔ S3/R2 gerenciado (troca por env)"*. No other
  dependency. Storage swaps by environment, so the swap rule holds.
- [x] **Principle 2 — Tenancy is a property of the data:** thirteen collections declared in the
  registry; access returns constraints; `sameTenant` on every scoped relationship; nothing
  outside `lib/tenancy` touches the Local API. `publicRead` **widens** access and is therefore
  the highest-risk change in the feature — it joins the mutation-point set.
- [ ] **Principle 3 — Pure game rules:** not applicable, deliberately. This feature writes no
  XP (CLR-001); it records approvals for feature 005 to consume.
- [x] **Principle 4 — Design and content fidelity:** fields labelled PT-BR, code English; the
  admin is the team's surface (US7); no visual vocabulary is added — `@fablab/ui` is consumed.
- [x] **Principle 5 — Enumerated gates:** the gate set grows — upload verification, the
  reconciliation test, public-read isolation, and the locked-documents assertion. Security
  review is **mandatory** here: this feature carries the first upload surface.

## Risks & Mitigations

| Risk | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| `publicRead` leaks unpublished or cross-tenant rows | A public, silent cross-tenant leak — the failure feature 000 exists to prevent | It joins the `@isolation-mutation-point` set; the harness is extended **before** content exists; the `or` branch is tested from all four vantage points (anonymous, member, other-org member, master) |
| Presigned upload bypasses verification | An unverified object is served | Objects land in `quarantine/`, which is not publicly served; only a passing check moves them |
| Abandoned presigned uploads accumulate | Disk exhaustion — `tech-stack.md` names disk as failure number one | Bucket lifecycle rule; owned by this feature rather than left unowned |
| Counter drift | Card grids show wrong numbers, quietly | Reconciliation test in CI; the drift paths are named in Sketch 7 |
| `imageSizes` misbehaves with direct upload | Thumbnails silently absent | **Unresolved — see below.** `tech-stack.md` requires this spike *before* the 002 spec is fixed |
| Thirteen collections at once | A template error replicated twelve times | One collection end to end first, then the rest |

## Open, and it belongs to the PO

`tech-stack.md` § *Absorções do benchmark* item 3 asks for a spike **before this spec is
fixed**: *"Validar também o comportamento real de `imageSizes` com upload direto antes de fixar
a spec da feature 002."* It has not been run. Either it runs before `/speckit.tasks`, or
`imageSizes` leaves the plan and thumbnails are generated another way. The plan does not assume
an answer.

## Quick Start

1. Run the `imageSizes` spike, or decide to drop it.
2. `publicRead` + `teamOnly` in `access.ts`, harness extended, mutation points marked — before
   any collection exists to use them.
3. `projeto` end to end as the template: registry, relations, review queue, counters.
4. Uploads: adapter, limits, quarantine, verification, reaper.
5. The remaining twelve collections against the proven template.
6. `payload-locked-documents`: the failing test first, then the fix.
